ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: The data collection protocol was approved by the University of Ottawa Research Ethics Board (#H 09-15-10).
All participants provided written informed consent prior to participation.
Participants with hearing loss were recruited from the clientele attending the clinic.
Participants in the normal-audiogram group were recruited through a general email announcement distributed by the program secretariat to staff and program collaborators.

As summarized in Table 1, participants had, on average, a sloping hearing loss, with mean thresholds ranging from the mild hearing loss range at 1 kHz to the moderately severe hearing loss range at 8 kHz in their better-hearing ear.
table.formatted: As summarized in Table <ref type="table" target="#tab_0">1</ref>, participants had, on average, a sloping hearing loss, with mean thresholds ranging from the mild hearing loss range at 1 kHz to the moderately severe hearing loss range at 8 kHz in their better-hearing ear.

table.text: Participants were instructed to repeat the word presented after the warning beep and to guess when unsure.
SRTinN estimates for individual participants are presented in Tables 1 and 2.
table.formatted: SRTinN estimates for individual participants are presented in Tables <ref type="table" target="#tab_0">1</ref> and <ref type="table" target="#tab_1">2</ref>.

ethics_check.report:

> Participants in the normal-audiogram group were recruited through a general email announcement distributed by the program secretariat to staff and program collaborators.

> As summarized in Table 1, participants had, on average, a sloping hearing loss, with mean thresholds ranging from the mild hearing loss range at 1 kHz to the moderately severe hearing loss range at 8 kHz in their better-hearing ear.

> Participants were instructed to repeat the word presented after the warning beep and to guess when unsure.

> SRTinN estimates for individual participants are presented in Tables 1 and 2.

Ethics approval statement:

> The data collection protocol was approved by the University of Ottawa Research Ethics Board (#H 09-15-10).

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

stat_p_exact.title: Exact P-Values
stat_p_exact.summary_text: We found no imprecise *p* values, *p*-values of exactly zero or impossible *p* values out of 3 detected.

table.expanded: A Mann-Whitney U test indicated a significant difference in SRTinN between participants with hearing loss and those with normal audiograms (U = 31.5, p = 0.02).

table.header: Association between SRTinN and pure-tone thresholds
table.expanded: Among participants with hearing loss, SRTinN was significantly correlated with conventional PTA (r = 0.54, p = 0.04), corresponding to 29% shared variance (R² = 0.29).

table.header: Association between SRTinN and pure-tone thresholds
table.expanded: A descriptively stronger association was observed between SRTinN and HFPTA (r = 0.64, p = 0.01), corresponding to 41% shared variance (R² = 0.41).
